deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is an observing-log page with a latitude determination from Polaris (α Ursae minoris) near its LOWER culmination, observed on 22 March. The bundle date, the repeating-circle technique, the Shelton and Kampe clocks, and Polaris' apparent declination of about 88°18'40" all point to Göttingen around 1813–15, before the new observatory. The page continues the 20 March series on the previous page and is continued on 26 and 31 March on the next page. The instrument is a repeating circle (a Reichenbach-type circle, read cumulatively).

1) Clock time of culmination (top right). Apparent RA of Polaris = 0h54m48.44s, plus the clock correction +6m52.2s, minus the Kampe–Shelton difference 1m33s, gives 1h0m7.64s ≈ 1h0m8s. Since lower culmination occurs at RA+12h of sidereal time, the clock reading of lower culmination is 13h0m08s. The clock comparison at the foot of the page supports this: Kampe − Shelton = −1'32.5" at 12h33m and −1'33.5" at 13h29m.

2) Hour angles (second time column). Each is t = |T − 13h0m08s|:
- 12h40m37s gives 19m31s.
- 13h20m19s gives 20m11s.
- All 18 entries check.

3) Reduction to the meridian (decimal column). Each value is r = A·2 sin²(t/2)/sin1", with A = cosφ cosδ / sin z ≈ 0.6218·0.02948/0.6449 ≈ 0.0284. My check gives:
- t = 19m31s (17565") → 21.26"; Gauss has 21.25.
- t = 1m12s → 0.08".
- t = 20m11s → 22.73"; Gauss has 22.72.
At lower culmination the zenith distance is a maximum, so the reductions are added. The second-order term is negligible.

4) Repeating-circle readings. These are cumulative readings after n = 4, 6, 8, 12 and 18 pointings. For each, Gauss adds the running sum of reductions and divides by n:
- n=4: 160°33'26" + 57.69" = 160°34'23.7"; ÷4 = 40°8'36.0".
- n=6: 240°50'17" + 63.65" = 240°51'20.65"; ÷6 = 40°8'33.4" (he writes 33.5).
- n=8: 321°7'24" + 64.79" = 321°8'28.8"; ÷8 = 40°8'33.6".
- n=12: 481°41'39" + 69.62" = 481°42'48.6"; ÷12 = 40°8'34.05".
- n=18: 722°32'3.25" + 149.30" = 722°34'32.55"; ÷18 = 40°8'35.14".
The last value is the adopted apparent meridian zenith distance.

5) Refraction and latitude.
- Barometer 27 Paris inches 8.3 lines, thermometer +1.25° (Réaumur). Refraction at z ≈ 40°8.6' is taken as 50.05" (mean ≈ 57.7"·tan z, corrected for density).
- True z = 40°8'35.14" + 50.05" = 40°9'25.19".
- With apparent declination δ = 88°18'39.72", lower culmination gives φ = 180° − z − δ = 51°31'55.09".

6) Combination with the previous series. The 20 March value was 51°31'54.39" from 10 observations. The weighted mean is (10·54.39 + 18·55.09)/28 = 54.84", so φ = 51°31'54.84" from 28 observations. The next page carries 28 → 54.84 forward.

The marginal numbers at the left edge belong to the facing page (17 March γ Cephei series and the word 'Culmination').
errors: No computational errors found. All 18 hour angles, the cumulative reduction sums (57.69, 63.65, 64.79, 69.62, 149.30), the divisions by n, the refraction addition and 180° − z − δ all check.
Minor rounding only: 240°51'20.65"/6 = 40°8'33.44" is written as 33.5.
The left column '13 1.20' etc. continues the hour 13 (13h1m20s, …), not a separate count.

results.what: Reduction of circum-meridian zenith distances to the meridian: r = cosφ cosδ / sin z · 2 sin²(t/2)/sin1", applied to Polaris at lower culmination
results.usually_credited_to: 18th-century practice (Delambre's tables; Borda/Mendez for repeating circles)

results.what: Latitude from Polaris at lower culmination: φ = 180° − z − δ, with refraction correction
results.modern_name: Latitude determination by circumpolar star at lower culmination

results.what: Weighted mean of two series by number of observations: 28 observations give 51°31'54.84"
Repeating-circle cumulative readings divided by number of repetitions

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine observing-log computation of Göttingen's latitude from Polaris with a repeating circle. Gauss's latitude work at Göttingen is well documented, and nothing here is mathematically novel.

checkable.asserts: 0h54m48.44s + 6m52.2s - 1m33s, expressed in seconds minus 1 h, equals 7.64 s, i.e. culmination at 1h0m8s (clock reading 13h0m08s)
Reduction for t = 19m31s is about 21.25 arcsec
Reduction for t = 20m11s is about 22.72 arcsec
The total of the 18 reductions is 149.30 arcsec
The mean meridian zenith distance excess over 40° is 515.142 arcsec, i.e. 40°8'35.14"
The weighted mean of the two series is 54.84 arcsec

transcription_corrections: The final line '28 54"34' should read 28 → 54"84: the weighted mean (10·54.39 + 18·55.09)/28 = 54.84, and the next page repeats '28 54,84'.
The struck-out entry beside 52 10 is a cancelled premature writing of the 240.50.17 reading.
'2\12' in the hour-angle column is 2m12s (12h57m56s → 2m12s to 13h0m08s).
The 'Shelton Kampe' entries are clock comparisons (Kampe − Shelton = −1m32.5s at 12h33m, −1m33.5s at 13h29m).
